A1_1.evidence: HTTPS delivery from an open-access article - 'This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)' (p. 1), pack licence cc-by-4.0, HTTP 200 - is open, free, and universally implementable. No subscription, proprietary client, or paywall stands between a reader and the supplementary scripts.

I1.evidence: The code is source in a formal, shared, broadly applicable language: 'All analyses were undertaken in "R" version 4.3.0. I3.evidence: Third-party dependencies enter code scoring only through citation quality, and none is cited: no R package is named, versioned, or cited anywhere (only the base 'R version 4.3.0'), and no software DOI or typed relation is given. The OLE literature cited (Roberts and Solow 2003; Clements et al. 2013; Rivadeneira et al. 2009) is methodological, cited bibliographically and without PIDs, not as qualified references from the code artefact.

R1.evidence: The code is described by a plurality of relevant attributes reachable from the paper: purpose and scope ('the script used to run all validation analyses'; 'the script used to run all case study tests'), language and version ('R' version 4.3.0), and fully specified parameters - k values 'of 5, 20 and 30 for all validation tests' extended to 'using 5, 10, 20 and 30 records', subsampling 'at rates of 5%, 10%, 20%, and 50% relative to the total number of records', 'One thousand iterations of each process were performed', results 'presented as median values across all iterations', and the alpha ('with alpha of 0.05 used here'). Missing README/installation instructions are noted as a gap, but the guide admits a methods description as qualifying documentation.

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified, not merely a platform field: the article is CC BY 4.0 ('This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)', p. 1), and under v2.1 the article licence extends to publisher-hosted supplements absent a separate supplement licence. The pack's licence-conflict check for declared_id 'supplement' records paper_asserted 'CC BY' against service_recorded 'cc-by-4.0' with 'conflict': false, so the most-restrictive rule is not triggered; the co-recorded Elsevier TDM licences are text-and-data-mining route terms, not a competing content licence.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed computational provenance is documented: software version ('R' version 4.3.0); the full analytical pipeline (random subsampling of the replica assemblages at stated rates, entry of only the k largest or smallest values, 1000 iterations, medians reported, T_E and T_CI outputs defined); transformations and data-conditioning decisions ('all duplicates were automatically removed before the validation analyses', and the Sect. 2.4.1.6.1 resampling of each value 'from a normal distribution, where we used the value itself as the mean, and a very small standard deviation (0.001)'); and attribution of the analytic work through CRediT (Alastair Key: Formal analysis, Methodology, Validation; Alfredo Cortell-Nicolau: Formal analysis; Ivan Jaric: Formal analysis, Methodology). Gap noted: no random seed is reported despite stochastic subsampling.

R1_3.evidence: No deposit-level code standard is met: the artefact is a bare supplementary script, with no package structure, no CITATION.cff, no CodeMeta, and no community review route (not on CRAN, JOSS, or rOpenSci) - none is claimed in the paper and Row 6 grants no such entitlement. The standards the paper invokes (OLE per Roberts and Solow 2003; k-value recommendations per Solow 2005 and Rivadeneira et al. 2009) are methodological and expressly excluded by v2.1.

A1_1.evidence: Protocol quality for the accessible portion: the descriptive and range data that are published (Table 1 replica-assemblage means/SD/CV/min/max; Tables 5-7 per-variable range data for every case study; Supplementary Tables 1-3) are served over HTTPS from an open-access article - 'This is an open access article under the CC BY license' (p. 1) - and the pack resolves the article record at HTTP 200 with licence cc-by-4.0. The protocol is open, free, and universally implementable; no paid subscription or proprietary client is required.

A1_2.evidence: v2.1 open case: the accessible portion is fully open and requires no authentication (open-access CC BY article and its publisher-served supplement; pack http_status 200). No access-control mechanism exists over the accessible portion, and no restriction is asserted or warranted on ethical grounds (no human-subjects or CARE-relevant material - the data are artefact measurements). Score 0 is reserved for undocumented/unjustified access control, which is not the case here.

A2.evidence: No metadata record exists for any dataset that could persist independently of the data (F2 = 0), so there is nothing to remain accessible if the resource became unavailable. No tombstone-bearing repository (Zenodo, DANS) is used; the paper names no repository at all.

F1.evidence: No dataset carries a globally unique persistent identifier. No repository, accession, or dataset DOI appears in the paper; there is no data availability statement. The datasets are referenced only through methods citations (e.g. Sect. 2.4.1.2: 'The methods used to collect these data can be viewed in Key and Lycett (2017)'). The F1 supplement route does not apply: only code is stated to be in the supplement ('The script used to run all case study tests is available in the supplementary information', Sect. 2.4), never the morphometric data. The article DOI in the pack describes the journal article, not a dataset.

F2.evidence: No independent artefact-level metadata record exists for any dataset, because nothing is deposited. The evidence pack holds a single record, a Crossref record of type 'journal-article' (publisher 'Elsevier BV'); it carries no dataset-level metadata. Rung (ii) is silent: no listed platform row is engaged for data, and Row 6 (publisher supplement) would in any case give F2 = 0.

F3.evidence: With no artefact-level metadata record for any dataset (F2 = 0), no such record can carry a dataset identifier. The pack's 'identifier_in_metadata: true' pertains to the article's Crossref record (doi 10.1016/j.jas.2023.105921), i.e. the article, not to any data artefact.

F4.evidence: No dataset is indexed in any searchable registry. Nothing is deposited in Zenodo, DataCite, or a domain registry (ADS, tDAR, DANS, Open Context) - none is named in the paper. The only registry indexing evidenced is the Crossref record for the article itself.

I1.evidence: The principal datasets - per-artefact morphometric records for each of the 13 assemblages - are not released in any format, so no formal, shared knowledge representation is evidenced. What is accessible appears only as typeset tables in the article PDF (Tables 1-7), i.e. human-readable, not machine-actionable; no CSV/JSON/XML dataset with a schema is claimed.

I2.evidence: No controlled vocabulary or ontology is used or cited for the data. Variables are ad hoc field names defined in prose and table headers - 'Length', 'Breadth', 'Thickness', 'Mass', 'Elongation', 'Refinement' (footnoted as 'the relative thickness of a tool (thickness divided by breadth)', Table 1), 'PC1', 'PC2'. No ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM, Getty AAT, PeriodO, or Darwin Core term is referenced anywhere.

I3.evidence: No dataset metadata record exists to carry qualified references. Upstream sources are cited as publications, not as data resources with PIDs and typed relations - e.g. 'Data are derived from Buchanan and Hamilton's (2021) study of scaling laws in Paleoindian projectile point design' (Sect. 2.4.1.5) points to an article, not a dataset identifier; the reference list gives bibliographic entries, overwhelmingly without DOIs. No 'is derived from [DOI]' style machine-actionable linkage is present.

R1.evidence: Every principal dataset is described with a plurality of relevant attributes (conjunctive test satisfied). Table 1 gives mean, SD, CV, minimum and maximum for all measured variables of both validation assemblages, with units stated ('Length, breadth, and thickness values are in millimetres (mm), while mass is in grams (g)'); Sects. 2.3.1-2.4.4 describe each case study by site, region, chronology, raw material, sample size, measured variables and selection criteria (e.g. 'we limit the present case study to the whole flakes excavated from MIS 15 sediments in the 2020 season (n = 173)'; microliths 'that preserve at least 95% of their original size'); Tables 5-7 report n, mean, minimum and maximum per variable per assemblage. The guide's operationalisation explicitly admits a methods description as qualifying documentation.

R1_1.evidence: No data usage licence attaches to any principal dataset, because none is released: there is no data availability statement and no deposit. The article's CC BY 4.0 (p. 1; pack service-recorded 'cc-by-4.0') extends to the article and its publisher-hosted supplement, but the supplement is stated to contain the analysis scripts, not the morphometric records. Under conjunctive data scoring, an unreleased and unlicensed principal dataset forces 0.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance is documented for each dataset: who created it and when ('500 replica Acheulean handaxes were produced by Key and Lycett (2017) over the course of 18 months'; Early Archaic points 'were originally knapped by M.I.E. in 2021', now 'curated at the Kent State University Experimental Archaeology Laboratory'); excavation context ('n = 134) is part of a larger LCT assemblage from Olduvai Gorge Beds III and IV (ca.1300-600 ka) excavated by Mary Leakey and colleagues between the 1969 and 1971 (n = 562)'); measurement process ('measured using diameter boards with 1 cm increments, callipers and a metal rule'; 'metric data were recorded in centimetres from plan-view and profile-view digital images'); processing steps (duplicate removal; the randomisation procedure of Sect. 2.4.1.6.1 with SD 0.001 over 1000 iterations); funding/collection responsibility in the Acknowledgements; and 'In all cases, morphometric data were collected prior to the present study being conceived.'

R1_3.evidence: No deposit-level community standard is met: no generic schema (DataCite, Dublin Core) because there is no metadata record; no domain schema or vocabulary (ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM) is cited; and no accredited domain repository is used, so the graded Row 4 route is not engaged. The standards the paper does invoke are methodological (OLE per Roberts and Solow 2003; sampling procedures per Rivadeneira et al. 2009), which v2.1 expressly excludes from R1.3.
